evidence: Specific to this product: the 20-minute slot grid on / with per-slot 'Few left' (amber) and 'Full' (greyed) states and a 'N slots free on <day>' count (root/slot-chosen/1280-light.png); vehicle choice Car / Car with trailer / Van with a DRC- permit field and an info disclosure explaining where the permit comes from (vehicle/info-open/1280-light.png); waste checklist with the centre's own limits ('Rubble (up to four bags)', 'Mattresses (up to two)'); a DR- reference set large on /done.html with 'Show this at the gate, on your phone or on paper'.

Generic: the visual chrome (white header with a small bin glyph and the council name, pale grey-green page, bordered white cards, green filled primary button, red-bordered 'There is a problem' summary, inline step text '1. When 2. Vehicle and waste 3. Check and book') is the standard public-sector service pattern; swapping the words would serve any council booking service unchanged.

Category-guess test: the look is guessable from 'UK council online service' alone. Similar-prompt test: a capable generator given 'council tip slot booking' would land very close to this chrome; the specificity comes from the content and the slot-grid states, not from visual decisions.

unfinished: Identity is only the council name in bold plus a small outline bin glyph in the header; nothing else carries Dunmore or the recycling centre.

The reference DR-204117 on /done.html, the one thing a resident must show at the gate, is set as a bold heading inside a plain bordered card at the same weight as 'At the centre'; there is no focal treatment of the gate pass (done/default/1280-light.png).

At 1280 and 1440 the vehicle and confirm forms occupy the left ~610px and leave the right half of the content column empty; on /done.html the 'At the centre' card stops at half width beside a full-width reference card for no visible reason.
On /done.html at 1280 the footer ends at ~716px and a flat grey band fills the rest of the viewport.
The 'Few left' group sits above 'Morning' with no heading of its own, so the slot grid reads as three blocks of boxes with an unlabelled first block.

Selected states are faint: the chosen day ('Saturday 17') and chosen slot ('09:20') differ from neighbours only by a pale tint and a slightly darker border (root/slot-chosen/1280-light.png, 1440-dark.png).
Headings differ from body mainly in size and weight; one family throughout with no typographic moment.
evidence: First viewport on / (1280-light): a title, a lead sentence, a text step list, a row of outlined day buttons and a grid of identical outlined boxes; the first thing the eye lands on is the amber 'Few left' row, not the choice the resident has made.

Everything is orderly and legible, spacing is consistent, the dark theme is carefully mapped (root/slot-chosen/1440-dark.png) and the error summaries are well formed, so it is not unappealing; but it is a clean default service form with no element chosen to be looked at, which is 'plain' by the rubric.
For an operate flow this restraint is largely appropriate; the shortfall is on the done page, a read surface whose job (the gate pass) would justify a single strong moment and gets none.
